newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Ericsson rises on report.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Ericsson rises on report.

text.p: Swedish telecommunications equipment company Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson rose Friday to highlight trade in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).

Ericsson was up 3/8 to 35-3/8 and its volume put it among the most-active ADRs. The rise came after a Swedish newspaper reported the company expected to sell 50 million mobile phones in 2000 in an overall market of 300 million phones.

Brazilian telephone holding Telebras SA continued to rebound, rising 1-1/8 to 122-3/8. The stock had fallen amid allegations Brazilian Communications Minister Sergio Motta was linked to a vote-buying scandal in Congress.

Telebras "is kind of bouncing back after all these rumors and Motta's denying it," a trader said, who described trade in Latin American ADRs as slow ahead of Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Reserve on interest rates.
"Everybody is waiting to see what the Fed has to say Tuesday," he said.
Among other ADRs, Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp rose 1-7/8 to a 12-month high of 47 following overnight interest in Tokyo.
The stock and others driven by domestic demand drew investors attracted by the yen's strengthening against the dollar.
British drugs company SmithKline Beecham Plc fell 1-1/4 to 86-1/8.
Advancers led decliners 218 to 206 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group rose 0.03 percent and volume in late morning was 23 million ADRs.
